topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series, outlines key learning outcomes, and establishes the clinical and biological framework for studying cancer.

topics.label: Biological nature and experimental modeling of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the core biological definition of cancer as a multistep disease of genetic alterations and disrupted tissue differentiation while examining the strengths and limits of cellular models.

topics.label: Distinguishing, classifying, and diagnosing benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the morphological, histological, and taxonomic criteria used to distinguish benign tumors from invasive and metastatic malignancies.

topics.label: Mechanisms of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the specific physical and physiological mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors impair normal tissue function and cause patient death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence across humans and other animal species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine patterns of tumor frequency and tissue distribution across human demographics and diverse multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical implementation of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the diagnostic rationale, cellular markers, and practical effectiveness of screening strategies across different cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding framing for the lecture, summarizing the session and directing students toward practical work.
